name: Tyran Stokes
notes:
Overview
Stokes is a polished, physical, multi-skilled forward whose value comes from doing several things well rather than relying on one scoring method. He creates advantages through strength, size, skill and decision-making, then either finishes himself or finds teammates when the defense reacts.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Can score at the rim, from the midrange, off the dribble and in transition; he is not dependent on one shot type.

Creation: Uses strength, size and skill to create advantages, then punishes help defenders with finishing or passing.

Playmaking: Passing is a real secondary skill; he finds teammates once defenders collapse.

Finishing: Physical at the rim, comfortable through contact and capable of drawing fouls.

Shooting: His high release gives him an advantage over smaller defenders, though consistency remains the key question.

Off-ball impact: Rebounds, runs the floor and benefits from spacing and ball movement.

Defensive evaluation

On-ball defense: His size, mobility and frame give him multi-position defensive potential.

Help defense: His 2.1 steals and 1.4 blocks show real defensive activity, not just physical tools.

Rebounding: 7.9 rebounds per game supports his ability to control possessions and start offense.

Versatility: Can match up with wings and bigger forwards, though consistent focus is the main question.

Strengths

Rare physical tools, strength and wing mobility.

Multi-level scoring and ability to finish through contact.

Rebounding, transition play and secondary playmaking.

Two-way potential from his length, activity and physical profile.

Weaknesses

Three-point consistency needs to become more reliable.

Half-court creation and decision-making are still developing.

Must bring more consistent defensive focus and discipline.

Tendencies

Preferred actions: Transition attacks, physical drives, post-related actions, offensive rebounds and kick-out passes.

Shot selection: Willing to shoot from multiple levels, but needs better consistency from deep.

Decision-making: Strong when attacking advantages, still developing control in half-court settings.

Defensive habits: Tools are high-level, but focus and discipline need to become more consistent.

Why the stats support the scout

18.2 points on 49.5% shooting shows efficient, high-level scoring.

7.9 rebounds and 4.3 assists match his rebound-and-push, driver-and-passer profile.

34.2% from three is promising but remains the main development area.

6.4 BPM, 2.1 steals and 1.4 blocks support genuine two-way impact.

Development plan

Make the three-point shot a more consistent, higher-volume weapon.

Improve controlled half-court creation and reduce loose turnovers.

Turn his physical tools into consistent defensive focus and discipline.

Opponent scouting notes

Force him into difficult half-court pull-ups rather than allowing straight-line drives.

Make him prove he can consistently make perimeter shots.

Use physical, disciplined closeouts and make him pass rather than finish.

Test his defensive focus with movement, screening and transition attacks.

Projection

Current role: High-usage freshman wing/forward with two-way upside.

NBA ceiling: Franchise-level scoring forward and potential top pick.

Realistic outcome: High-impact NBA starter if the jumper, half-court creation and defensive consistency develop.

Best fit: A spaced offence with a lead creator, allowing Stokes to attack closeouts, rebound and make secondary plays.

Bottom line
Stokes is not just an athlete or a transition scorer. He can drive, finish through contact, shoot over defenders, rebound, make reads and create for others. His 18.2/7.9/4.3 line and 6.4 BPM match that all-around profile. The gap between being a very good college player and a top NBA pick will come down to whether his jumper becomes reliable, his half-court game becomes more controlled, and he brings the same focus defensively every night.

name: Jordan Smith Jr.
notes:
Overview
Smith Jr. is a high-energy, two-way guard whose value comes from impacting the game in every phase: scoring, rebounding, playmaking, transition offense and defense. He sets the tone physically, turns defensive stops into offense and makes winning plays rather than simply hunting shots.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Comfortable finishing at the rim, attacking in transition and making timely perimeter shots.

Creation: More of a transition and secondary creator than a polished half-court initiator, but capable of making reads off defensive pressure.

Playmaking: 3.1 assists per game show real passing feel, especially in transition and after steals.

Finishing: Strong, explosive finisher who can absorb contact and convert in traffic.

Shooting: 31.0% from three is the main offensive question; he is willing to shoot but not yet consistently reliable.

Off-ball impact: Rebounds well for a guard, runs the floor hard and creates extra possessions through activity.

Defensive evaluation

On-ball defense: Physical, aggressive and capable of pressuring ball-handlers.

Help defense: 2.4 steals and 1.1 blocks show strong anticipation and activity beyond his position.

Rebounding: 5.2 rebounds per game is excellent for a guard and directly fuels his transition game.

Versatility: His strength, energy and defensive instincts give him potential to guard either backcourt spot.

Strengths

Elite motor, physicality and two-way competitiveness.

Transition scoring and ability to turn defense into offense.

All-around production: scoring, rebounding, playmaking and defensive activity.

Rim pressure and contact finishing.

Weaknesses

Three-point shooting needs to become more consistent.

Half-court creation and decision-making are still developing.

His game relies heavily on energy and transition; he must prove he can create efficiently in structured settings.

Tendencies

Preferred actions: Transition attacks, drives off steals, coast-to-coast finishes and secondary playmaking.

Shot selection: Willing to shoot from deep but still developing consistency.

Decision-making: Strong in transition, still refining half-court reads.

Defensive habits: Aggressive, active and disruptive, with a willingness to gamble for takeaways.

Why the stats support the scout

16.5 points on 46.8% shooting shows efficient scoring.

5.2 rebounds and 2.4 steals match the film’s physical, all-around profile.

3.1 assists support real secondary creation.

4.95 BPM reflects impact across multiple categories, not just scoring.

Development plan

Improve three-point consistency to become a legitimate spacing threat.

Develop tighter half-court handling and more controlled creation.

Maintain defensive intensity while reducing unnecessary gambling.

Opponent scouting notes

Force him into half-court sets and limit transition chances.

Make him prove he can consistently make open threes.

Use physical, disciplined closeouts and avoid careless passes that fuel his transition game.

Projection

Current role: High-impact freshman two-way guard.

NBA ceiling: Starting two-way combo guard with All-Defensive potential.

Realistic outcome: High-energy rotation guard whose value comes from defense, transition and winning plays.

Best fit: Next to a shooting lead guard, in a pressure defensive system that plays fast.

Bottom line
Smith Jr. is not just a scorer; he is a complete energy player who affects possessions on both ends. His 16.5/5.2/3.1 line, 2.4 steals and 4.95 BPM match his physical, transition-heavy, winning style. If his three-point shot becomes reliable and his half-court creation matures, he has a clear path to being a high-level NBA guard.

name: Caleb Holt
notes:
Overview
Holt is a versatile, physical shooting guard who impacts the game as a scorer, rebounder, passer and defender. He does not need his shot to fall to contribute: he attacks the rim, competes on the glass, makes simple reads and disrupts possessions defensively.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Productive multi-level scorer who can attack the rim and finish efficiently.

Creation: Capable of creating his own shot off the bounce, though he is more of a wing scorer than a full-time lead initiator.

Playmaking: 2.8 assists per game and his passing reads show useful secondary creation.

Finishing: Confident driver with the ability to finish through contact and create separation with footwork.

Shooting: 33.1% from three is workable but needs to improve for him to become a true high-level wing scorer.

Off-ball impact: Rebounds aggressively and finds ways to contribute when his shot is not falling.

Defensive evaluation

On-ball defense: Active, competitive and willing to take on tough assignments.

Help defense: 1.9 steals and 0.6 blocks show real defensive playmaking.

Rebounding: 6.5 rebounds per game is strong for a shooting guard.

Versatility: His size, activity and motor suggest he can defend multiple perimeter positions.

Strengths

All-around two-way production.

Rim pressure, physical finishing and offensive rebounding.

Defensive activity and ability to impact possessions without scoring.

Secondary playmaking and willingness to make the right read.

Weaknesses

Three-point shooting needs to become more consistent.

Not yet a proven primary creator in the half court.

Must continue developing shot selection and efficiency against higher-level defenses.

Tendencies

Preferred actions: Attacking closeouts, driving to the rim, offensive rebounding and transition play.

Shot selection: Willing to attack but needs to become more selective from deep.

Decision-making: Shows good awareness when defenders collapse, especially as a passer.

Defensive habits: Active hands, effort plays and willingness to disrupt possessions.

Why the stats support the scout

17.0 points on 48.0% shooting shows efficient scoring volume.

6.5 rebounds and 1.9 steals match his physical, all-around profile.

33.1% from three is promising but still a development area.

5.1 BPM reflects broad, two-way impact.

Development plan

Improve three-point consistency and expand his range.

Develop more advanced half-court creation and pull-up shooting.

Continue building strength and defensive discipline against elite athletes.

Opponent scouting notes

Force him into contested perimeter shots rather than allowing straight-line drives.

Make him prove he can create consistently in the half court.

Box out aggressively and limit his second-chance opportunities.

Projection

Current role: High-usage freshman two-way shooting guard.

NBA ceiling: Starting two-way wing guard with two-way impact.

Realistic outcome: Versatile rotation guard who scores, defends and rebounds.

Best fit: Next to a primary creator, in a system that values transition, spacing and defensive activity.

Bottom line
Holt’s value is his versatility. He can score, rebound, pass and defend, and he impacts games even when his shooting is not at its best. His 17.0 points, 6.5 rebounds and 5.1 BPM support that all-around profile. The next step is turning his promising three-point shooting into a consistent weapon and developing more reliable half-court creation.

name: Stefan Joksimovic
notes:
Overview
Joksimovic is a Slovenian guard/wing whose game is built around transition scoring, perimeter shooting, timely defense and late-game confidence. He repeatedly turns defensive stops into offense and impacts games through energy, shooting and decisive plays.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Can score at the rim, from three, off screens and in late-clock situations.

Creation: Best when attacking in transition or using momentum after defensive stops; his half-court creation is still developing.

Playmaking: 5.5 assists per game suggests real connective ability, though he is more of a scorer and transition playmaker than a pure floor general.

Finishing: Strong finisher in transition, capable of dunking with force and scoring through contact.

Shooting: 35.8% from three supports legitimate perimeter spacing potential.

Off-ball impact: Can relocate, shoot off kick-outs and run the floor after defensive stops.

Defensive evaluation

On-ball defense: Active and competitive, with the ability to disrupt passing lanes.

Help defense: His transition defense and ability to create stops feed directly into his offense.

Rebounding: 3.9 rebounds per game is modest but acceptable for a guard/wing.

Versatility: His size and skill set give him potential to defend multiple perimeter positions.

Strengths

Transition scoring and ability to turn defense into offense.

Perimeter shooting and willingness to take big shots.

Late-game confidence and ability to make decisive plays.

Size and versatility for a guard/wing.

Weaknesses

Limited senior-level EuroLeague production makes his translation uncertain.

Half-court creation and consistency need further development.

Must prove his shooting and playmaking hold up against stronger, more physical professional defenses.

Tendencies

Preferred actions: Transition attacks, catch-and-shoot threes, drives off steals and late-clock shot-making.

Shot selection: Willing to shoot from deep and take important shots.

Decision-making: Strong in transition, still developing as a controlled half-court creator.

Defensive habits: Active in passing lanes and effective at converting turnovers into offense.

Why the stats support the scout

14.8 points and 45.1% shooting show productive scoring.

5.5 assists suggest real playmaking value.

35.8% from three supports his perimeter threat.

His modest BPM reflects that he is still establishing himself at the senior level.

Development plan

Earn consistent senior minutes and prove his production translates.

Improve half-court creation and decision-making.

Maintain shooting efficiency against higher-level defensive pressure.

Opponent scouting notes

Limit transition opportunities and avoid careless turnovers.

Force him into difficult half-court creations.

Run him off the three-point line and make him finish over length.

Projection

Current role: Young international guard/wing still establishing a professional role.

NBA ceiling: Big combo creator with shooting and transition upside.

Realistic outcome: Developmental European guard whose draft stock depends on earning real Baskonia minutes.

Best fit: A patient European development environment with spaced lineups and opportunities to play through mistakes.

Bottom line
Joksimovic is an intriguing international prospect because his game shows shooting, transition scoring, defensive activity and late-game confidence. His dataset numbers suggest real creation and shooting ability, but his limited EuroLeague sample means the main question is translation. If he earns consistent senior minutes and maintains his efficiency, he has a clear developmental path toward NBA consideration.

name: Bruce Branch III
notes:
Overview
Branch III is a long, skilled wing whose value goes beyond scoring. He contributes as a shooter, rebounder, passer and transition player, showing the type of all-around profile that fits a modern NBA wing.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Efficient wing scorer with a smooth perimeter shot.

Creation: More of a connector and secondary creator than a dynamic self-creator at this stage.

Playmaking: 2.1 assists per game and his passing reads show real feel for a wing.

Finishing: Can finish in transition and around the basket, though he is not yet an elite rim-pressure player.

Shooting: 38.0% from three is his clearest NBA-translatable skill.

Off-ball impact: Moves well without the ball, rebounds his position and makes timely cuts.

Defensive evaluation

On-ball defense: Length and fluidity give him potential to bother wings and smaller forwards.

Help defense: 1.4 steals per game shows active hands and awareness.

Rebounding: 4.8 rebounds per game is solid for a wing.

Versatility: His 6-7 frame and wingspan give him multi-position defensive upside.

Strengths

Perimeter shooting and smooth mechanics.

Length, mobility and two-way wing tools.

Playmaking feel and ability to make advanced passes.

All-around contribution beyond scoring.

Weaknesses

Needs to add strength to handle physical college and professional wings.

Not yet a consistent self-creator or pull-up shooter.

Must prove he can maintain production against higher-level, more physical competition.

Tendencies

Preferred actions: Spot-up shooting, transition play, cuts, secondary playmaking and effort plays.

Shot selection: Comfortable shooting from the perimeter and willing to take open threes.

Decision-making: Shows confidence making difficult passes and transition reads.

Defensive habits: Active, long and capable of creating turnovers.

Why the stats support the scout

13.9 points on 47.2% shooting shows efficient wing scoring.

38.0% from three is his strongest statistical indicator.

4.8 rebounds and 2.1 assists match his all-around film profile.

3.8 BPM reflects positive impact across categories.

Development plan

Add strength and physical maturity.

Develop a more consistent pull-up and self-creation package.

Continue improving defensive discipline and consistency.

Opponent scouting notes

Force him into physical matchups and test his strength.

Make him create off the dribble rather than allowing easy catch-and-shoot looks.

Close out hard and contest his three-point attempts.

Projection

Current role: Versatile freshman wing with shooting and connective skills.

NBA ceiling: Starting 3-and-D wing with secondary creation upside.

Realistic outcome: Long, skilled rotation wing whose value starts with shooting, length and team play.

Best fit: Next to a primary creator, in a system that values spacing, movement and transition.

Bottom line
Branch III’s profile is built around shooting, length and all-around feel. His 38.0% three-point shooting, 4.8 rebounds and 2.1 assists match his versatile wing profile. His ceiling depends on adding strength and developing more consistent self-creation, but his current skill set already fits a modern NBA wing role.

name: Anthony Thompson
notes:
Overview
Thompson is a confident, versatile forward who functions as a primary offensive option and vocal leader. He can score off the bounce, attack closeouts, make reads out of ball screens and impact the game defensively through effort and activity.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Versatile scorer who can attack off the bounce, score in isolation and finish at the rim.

Creation: Genuine creation ability, especially in ball-screen and isolation situations.

Playmaking: 1.8 assists per game understates his passing feel; he shows solid vision, short-pocket passes and kick-outs.

Finishing: Aggressive driver who seeks contact and gets to the line.

Shooting: 36.5% from three is promising, but his volume and consistency need to grow.

Off-ball impact: Can attack closeouts and operate as a secondary connector.

Defensive evaluation

On-ball defense: Plays with intensity and applies pressure to ball-handlers.

Help defense: Shows instincts rotating and helping in the paint.

Rebounding: 6.2 rebounds per game reflects solid effort and positioning.

Versatility: His size and mobility give him frontcourt versatility, though pick-and-roll coverage needs work.

Strengths

Versatile scoring package and confidence as a primary option.

Ball-handling, creation and ability to make reads under pressure.

High motor, leadership and competitiveness.

Rim protection and defensive activity.

Weaknesses

Shot selection can be inconsistent, especially with contested midrange attempts.

Three-point volume and efficiency need to improve.

Left-hand finishing and pick-and-roll defense remain development areas.

Needs added strength to finish consistently against bigger, stronger defenders.

Tendencies

Preferred actions: Attacking closeouts, driving right, midrange pull-ups and kick-outs after drawing help.

Shot selection: Confident but sometimes forces difficult shots.

Decision-making: Generally sound, with good late-clock awareness.

Defensive habits: High effort, but can overcommit in pick-and-roll coverage and transition.

Why the stats support the scout

12.4 points on 51.0% shooting shows efficient scoring.

36.5% from three supports real stretch potential.

6.2 rebounds and 1.5 blocks match his physical, two-way profile.

4.2 BPM reflects positive all-around impact.

Development plan

Improve three-point consistency and volume.

Develop left-hand finishing and better shot selection.

Improve pick-and-roll defense, transition awareness and foul discipline.

Opponent scouting notes

Force him to his left hand and make him finish through contact.

Take away his midrange pull-up with physical closeouts.

Test his three-point consistency and force him to facilitate rather than score.

Projection

Current role: Primary freshman forward and go-to scorer.

NBA ceiling: Versatile scoring forward with playmaking and defensive upside.

Realistic outcome: High-upside wing/forward whose NBA value depends on shooting, strength and defensive consistency.

Best fit: A system that gives him creation responsibility, spacing and opportunities to play through ball screens.

Bottom line
Thompson is a dynamic, confident forward who impacts both ends. The film shows real creation, passing feel, scoring versatility and defensive effort, while his 12.4 points, 36.5% three-point shooting and 4.2 BPM support that profile. His ceiling depends on becoming a more selective shooter, improving his left hand and cleaning up defensive details.

name: Quentin Coleman
notes:
Overview
Coleman is a high-motor, physical guard/forward who plays bigger than his size and impacts the game through rebounding, interior finishing, passing and competitive defense. He is a two-way connector who initiates offense off drives and offensive rebounds while creating opportunities for teammates.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Best around the rim and in the midrange, with a developing three-point shot.

Creation: More of a secondary initiator than a true lead guard, but capable of creating off drives and offensive rebounds.

Playmaking: 4.9 assists per game and his passing reads show real connective value.

Finishing: Strong, physical finisher who plays through contact and converts second-chance opportunities.

Shooting: 32.7% from three is workable but must improve for him to become a true floor spacer.

Off-ball impact: Elite rebounder for his size who creates extra possessions and generates offense off the glass.

Defensive evaluation

On-ball defense: Active, physical and capable of bothering ball-handlers with strength and length.

Help defense: Strong rotational awareness and willingness to contest shots.

Rebounding: One of his best traits; he secures contested boards and initiates transition.

Versatility: Can battle bigger opponents using leverage, though quicker wings may give him problems.

Strengths

Elite motor, toughness and competitiveness.

Rebounding, second-chance scoring and ability to create offense off the glass.

Physical finishing and midrange scoring.

Defensive communication, positioning and willingness to take charges.

Weaknesses

Three-point consistency is the biggest offensive development area.

Can force tough contested shots under pressure instead of resetting.

Lateral quickness against elite wings needs improvement.

Needs tighter handling in trapping and pressure situations.

Tendencies

Preferred actions: Drives, offensive rebounds, putbacks, short-roll play and midrange pull-ups.

Shot selection: Willing to shoot from deep but still developing consistency.

Decision-making: Good feel for rotations and help-side passing, though he can force shots when double-teamed.

Defensive habits: Physical, engaged and strong communicator.

Why the stats support the scout

11.4 points, 4.1 rebounds and 4.9 assists show a genuine all-around connector.

1.8 steals supports his active defensive profile.

32.7% from three is the main offensive development area.

3.1 BPM reflects positive impact beyond scoring.

Development plan

Improve three-point consistency and catch-and-shoot reliability.

Develop tighter ball-handling and better decision-making under pressure.

Improve lateral quickness and closeout discipline.

Opponent scouting notes

Force him to shoot from deep and prove his range.

Use quicker wings to attack him in space.

Make him handle pressure and create against traps rather than allowing easy offensive rebounds.

Projection

Current role: High-energy freshman connector and secondary initiator.

NBA ceiling: Versatile 3-and-D forward with secondary creation upside.

Realistic outcome: Physical, high-motor rotation forward whose value comes from rebounding, defense and winning plays.

Best fit: A ball-movement system that lets him attack closeouts, rebound and operate in short-roll situations.

Bottom line
Coleman is a physical, high-motor connector who plays bigger than his size. His 11.4 points, 4.1 rebounds, 4.9 assists and 1.8 steals match his all-around, two-way profile. His NBA path depends on becoming a more consistent shooter and improving his lateral mobility, but his toughness, rebounding and feel give him a clear developmental foundation.

name: Colben Landrew
notes:
Overview
Landrew is a modern scoring wing with strong perimeter offense, good transition pace and developing playmaking instincts. He projects as a multi-positional floor spacer who can shoot from deep, attack in transition and make simple reads, while still needing to grow as an on-ball defender and half-court creator.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Best as a spot-up shooter and transition scorer, with growing pull-up potential.

Creation: Can attack closeouts and create rhythm shots, but not yet a consistent primary creator.

Playmaking: 1.9 assists per game and his passing instincts show useful connective value.

Finishing: Capable in transition, though his finishing package is less developed than his shooting.

Shooting: 34.0% from three in your dataset, with stronger shooting indicators in the film, makes spacing his core skill.

Off-ball impact: Excellent relocation, cutting and movement without the ball.

Defensive evaluation

On-ball defense: Shows effort and the ability to contest shots, but needs more strength.

Help defense: Needs improvement in awareness and rotations.

Rebounding: 5.0 rebounds per game is solid for a wing.

Versatility: His size and mobility give him multi-positional potential, but physical development is key.

Strengths

Spot-up shooting and quick release.

Off-ball movement, cutting and relocation.

Transition scoring and intelligent pace.

Rhythm shot creation and developing passing instincts.

Weaknesses

Needs more strength and consistency as an on-ball defender.

Help-defense awareness and rotations need development.

Not yet a reliable primary creator in the half court.

Tendencies

Preferred actions: Catch-and-shoot threes, transition pulls, cuts and closeout attacks.

Shot selection: Generally disciplined, preferring rhythm shots over forced long twos.

Decision-making: Makes timely passes and reads the floor well off the ball.

Defensive habits: Competitive but still developing strength and awareness.

Why the stats support the scout

13.1 points on 46.2% shooting shows efficient wing scoring.

34.0% from three supports his spacing profile.

5.0 rebounds and 1.9 assists match his movement and connective style.

2.9 BPM reflects positive all-around contribution.

Development plan

Add strength and improve on-ball defense.

Develop help-defense awareness and rotations.

Expand his pull-up game and half-court creation.

Opponent scouting notes

Run him off the three-point line and force him to create off the bounce.

Use physical wings to test his strength and defensive discipline.

Attack his help-defense positioning with movement and screening actions.

Projection

Current role: Freshman scoring wing and floor spacer.

NBA ceiling: Multi-positional 3-and-D wing with secondary creation upside.

Realistic outcome: Rotation wing whose value starts with shooting, movement and transition play.

Best fit: Next to a primary creator, in a spaced system that values ball movement and transition.

Bottom line
Landrew’s clearest NBA skill is shooting, but he also shows real off-ball feel, transition pace and developing playmaking. His 13.1 points, 34.0% three-point shooting and 2.9 BPM support a modern wing profile. His development depends on adding strength, improving defense and turning his shooting into a more complete creation package.

name: Luigi Suigo
notes:
Overview
Suigo is a 7-foot-3 Italian developmental center whose value comes from elite size, rim protection and finishing potential. He impacts the paint defensively while still developing the strength, shooting and feel needed for a larger professional role.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Best as a finisher around the basket, with limited self-creation at this stage.

Creation: Very limited; he needs others to create for him.

Playmaking: 0.4 assists per game shows minimal passing value.

Finishing: 49.2% from the field supports solid interior finishing, though his efficiency needs to rise with more consistent minutes.

Shooting: 27.8% from three shows willingness but not yet reliability.

Off-ball impact: Can screen, roll, occupy space and create second-chance opportunities through size.

Defensive evaluation

On-ball defense: His size gives him a natural advantage protecting the paint.

Help defense: 1.8 blocks per game shows real rim-protection impact.

Rebounding: 4.8 rebounds per game is modest for his size and needs to grow.

Versatility: His length is elite, but his mobility and ability to defend in space need film confirmation.

Strengths

Rare 7-foot-3 size and length.

Rim protection and shot-blocking.

Interior finishing potential.

Willingness to develop perimeter shooting.

Weaknesses

Three-point accuracy is still far below a reliable NBA level.

Free-throw shooting needs improvement.

Limited playmaking and creation.

Needs to add strength and prove he can handle physical professional competition.

Tendencies

Preferred actions: Rim runs, putbacks, rolls, shot-blocking and occasional perimeter attempts.

Shot selection: Mostly interior, with early willingness to shoot from three.

Decision-making: Limited sample; needs more experience and polish.

Defensive habits: Strong rim protection but still developing overall defensive feel.

Why the stats support the scout

7.5 points and 49.2% shooting show efficient interior scoring.

1.8 blocks per game supports his rim-protection profile.

27.8% from three shows developmental shooting potential but not yet reliability.

5.6 BPM reflects meaningful impact despite limited minutes.

Development plan

Add strength and improve physical durability.

Improve three-point and free-throw shooting.

Develop passing, screening and defensive mobility.

Opponent scouting notes

Force him away from the rim and test his mobility.

Make him prove he can consistently make perimeter shots.

Attack him with quick, physical bigs and movement-heavy actions.

Projection

Current role: Developmental rim-protecting center.

NBA ceiling: Long-term stretch-center prospect with elite size.

Realistic outcome: Developmental big whose NBA relevance depends on shooting, strength and consistency.

Best fit: A patient European development role with spacing and creators around him.

Bottom line
Suigo’s profile is built on rare size, rim protection and developmental shooting potential. His 7.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.8 blocks and 5.6 BPM show real impact, but his limited playmaking and shooting accuracy mean he is still a long-term project. If he adds strength and becomes a more reliable shooter, his size gives him a unique NBA pathway.

name: Braylon Mullins
notes:
Overview
Mullins is a 6-6 shooting guard whose clearest NBA skill is shooting. He is an efficient, controlled scorer who spaces the floor, makes open shots and plays within a structured offensive role, while still needing to develop more creation and defensive versatility.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Efficient perimeter scorer with strong shooting mechanics and a clear scoring role.

Creation: More of a movement shooter and secondary creator than a lead initiator.

Playmaking: 2.5 assists per game shows basic connective ability, but not high-level creation.

Finishing: Capable of attacking closeouts, though his finishing package is less developed than his shooting.

Shooting: 41.2% from three in your dataset, and 88.9% from the line in UConn’s official data, make shooting his elite trait.

Off-ball impact: Strong relocation, spacing and ability to play off primary creators.

Defensive evaluation

On-ball defense: Needs film confirmation; his steal and block numbers are modest.

Help defense: Limited defensive playmaking in the current data.

Rebounding: 3.8 rebounds per game is acceptable for a shooting guard.

Versatility: His 6-6 size gives him positional potential, but his defensive impact is still unproven.

Strengths

Elite three-point shooting and free-throw touch.

Ideal 6-6 shooting-guard size.

Efficient, low-mistake scoring profile.

Ability to space the floor and play off primary creators.

Weaknesses

Limited creation and playmaking.

Defensive impact needs to develop.

Must prove he can create against longer, more athletic defenders.

Tendencies

Preferred actions: Catch-and-shoot threes, movement shooting, closeout attacks and simple reads.

Shot selection: Disciplined and efficient, with a clear preference for high-value shots.

Decision-making: Controlled and low-mistake, though not highly creative.

Defensive habits: Needs more consistent activity and impact.

Why the stats support the scout

15.3 points on 47.9% shooting shows efficient scoring.

41.2% from three is his clearest NBA-translatable skill.

7.2 BPM reflects strong positive impact.

2.5 assists and modest defensive numbers show he is more scorer than creator at this stage.

Development plan

Develop self-creation and pull-up shooting.

Improve defensive activity and versatility.

Expand his playmaking and ability to operate against pressure.

Opponent scouting notes

Run him off the three-point line and force him to create.

Use longer, more athletic defenders to test his finishing and handle.

Attack him defensively with movement and screening actions.

Projection

Current role: Freshman shooting guard and floor spacer.

NBA ceiling: Starting shooting guard with elite shooting and efficient scoring.

Realistic outcome: Rotation guard whose value starts with shooting, size and low-mistake play.

name: Thomas Haugh
notes:

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Comfortable finishing through contact around the rim, using hooks, up-and-under moves and putbacks.

Creation: Not a primary creator, but capable of attacking closeouts and making simple downhill plays.

Playmaking: Makes decisive passes on slips, pick-and-roll reads and short kick-outs.

Finishing: Physical finisher who draws fouls through aggressive drives and contact.

Shooting: 35.4% from three gives him real floor-spacing value, though he is not yet a high-volume deep shooter.

Off-ball impact: Strong cutter, offensive rebounder and second-chance scorer.

On-ball defense: Uses size and length well against forwards, though quicker guards can challenge him on switches.

Help defense: Effective rim deterrent with good angles, contests and rotations.

Rebounding: Active on both ends, using positioning and anticipation rather than relying only on athleticism.

Versatility: Can defend multiple frontcourt spots, though his lateral mobility is the main limitation.

Strengths

Interior scoring, physical finishing and foul-drawing.

Rebounding, hustle and second-chance impact.

Complementary three-point shooting and smart off-ball movement.

Team-oriented passing and late-game poise.

Weaknesses

Three-point consistency and volume need to improve.

Lateral quickness and footwork limit his switchability against smaller wings.

Limited self-creation off the dribble.

Preferred actions: Post touches, slips, short rolls, offensive rebounds and catch-and-shoot threes.

name: Jason Crowe Jr.
notes:
Overview
Crowe Jr. is a high-level scoring guard with elite shot-creation instincts, advanced ball-handling and confident late-game decision-making. He projects as a primary scorer who can also make plays for others, with his main development areas being efficiency, playmaking volume and defensive consistency.

Offensive evaluation

Scoring: Elite creator who can score off step-backs, pull-ups, floaters, euro-steps and creative finishes.

Creation: Advanced for his age; uses crossovers, hesitations and change-of-direction moves to beat defenders.

Playmaking: Good vision for a primary scorer, able to make reads when defenses collapse and run pick-and-roll actions.

Shooting: Reliable catch-and-shoot range with the ability to make pull-up threes, though 33.8% needs to become more consistent.

On-ball defense: Competitive with quick hands, lateral feet and strong anticipation.

Help defense: Generally solid, though he can have positioning lapses.

Rebounding: Active for his position, especially on the defensive glass.

Versatility: Can guard guards, but longer or stronger opponents may test him.

Strengths

Elite shot creation and advanced ball-handling.

Multi-level scoring, including floaters, pull-ups and contact finishes.

Confident late-game decision-making.

Competitive motor and willingness to carry an offensive load.

42.1% from the field needs to improve for a high-usage guard.

Playmaking volume must grow beyond 4.1 assists per game.

Improve field-goal efficiency and shot selection.

Expand playmaking and reduce turnovers under heavy usage.

Develop strength and defensive technique against bigger guards.

Make him prove he can create efficiently for others rather than forcing shots.

Realistic outcome: High-usage combo guard whose NBA value depends on efficiency and playmaking growth.

Best fit: A system that gives him pick-and-roll responsibility and lets him create in transition.

name: Cameron Williams
notes:

Williams is a high-motor frontcourt player whose value comes from efficiency, rebounding, rim protection and energy. He is not yet a polished creator or shooter, but his physical tools and activity give him a clear developmental path as a modern big.

name: Dylan Mingo
notes:

Help defense: 1.7 steals per game shows active hands and anticipation.

Rebounding: 3.4 rebounds per game is solid for a guard.

Advanced playmaking and pick-and-roll feel.

Active defensive hands and transition impact.

Three-point consistency needs to improve.

Perimeter lateral quickness needs development against shifty guards.

Shot selection can be refined, especially with contested midrange attempts.

Improve three-point consistency and catch-and-shoot reliability.

Develop lateral quickness and defensive discipline.

Force him into contested jump shots rather than allowing downhill drives.

Use quick, low-center-of-gravity guards to test his lateral defense.

NBA ceiling: Two-way lead guard with creation and pick-and-roll upside.

Realistic outcome: High-upside guard whose value depends on shooting consistency and decision-making.

Best fit: An up-tempo, pick-and-roll-heavy system that lets him initiate and create.

Bottom line
Mingo is a confident, downhill lead guard who can score, create and make plays for others. His 12.1 points, 4.6 assists, 35.0% three-point shooting and 3.4 BPM support that profile. name: Baba Oladotun
notes:

Size, length and wing versatility.

Three-level scoring potential and touch.

Footwork and ball skills.

39.1% three-point shooting and real spacing value.

name: Tounde Yessoufou

name: Stefan Vaaks
notes:

name: Billy Richmond
